_about: Real searches, held to the real bills they must and must not return. preflight reads this twice:
under --code the bills below are the fixture, with search_index.json (what their own analyses and
texts are about), run through the matcher build_pages cuts out of app.js; with site/idx and
site/sidx built, the same cases run over the real index of the term, where at_most catches a flood,
every term of the table is looked for in every term's titles and texts, and a retitled bill is reported.
Nothing here is typed. python3 build_search_index.py --fixture tests/search_cases.json copies every
bill's title, sponsor, committees and topic from site/idx, cuts search_index.json out of the term's
real search index for exactly these bills, and copies the text of the few bills listed under "texts"
into search_texts.json. Add a bill by naming its id in a case and running that: an invented title
must = the search has to list it. first = it has the reader's own word, so it is listed above every
must bill, which the table found. never = plainly about something else. at_most = a ceiling on the
real index. same = each group is two sides' words for one subject and must return one list.
Machine-judged, by reading titles and, where a title did not settle it, the bill's text. It is a
seed, not the person's reference: the person's own judgments belong in the bench.

cases.why: the person's example: nothing was returned; no title says lgbtq; the review, 1 October: SB 520's text is about breast reduction for pain and never mentions gender; its title alone listed it
the person's example: 162 bills titled transfer, transparency or transportation, or heard by a Transportation committee

no title says bathroom; four of the eight say 'lavatory' once, in the text, and nowhere else. A rent registry, a bill on shared facilities in rentals and one on dwellings over water mention a bathroom too, and say nothing of sex
the reader's own word first: the two titles that say restroom, then the table's
the person's example: HB 377 says hormone treatments, and both words had to match
the text of each covers athletic or sporting competition (read 1 October)
HB 232 names abortion only in its analysis
returned nothing: control had to match too
gun and its SYN group first, then the table's: the right to bear arms and the risk protection orders
one bill, about aquatic weeds, which has the reader's own word and stays first
a verb in -ize also finds legalizing and legalization
the reader's own word first, housing vouchers included; then the education freedom account bills
321 bills: every title with school, education or student in it
seven returned and six were 'adult'
both amendments are titled 'the adoption of tax laws'; their analysis says 'tax on personal income'. The seven low-income bills it used to list are never-bills
one bill, about snow and ice, which stays first; the nine on immigration enforcement were missed
the two titles that say so first
142 bills: every election bill of the term
33 bills about aid and air, none about artificial intelligence
34 bills about evidence, eviction and evaluation
a four-letter plural finds its singular
car, as a word: not care, not card
'law' carries no subject and was skipped, so this searched 'enforcement'
typed on a phone, with a curly apostrophe: none were found
HB 712's text says transgender and gender reassignment; SB 520, with the same words in its title, says neither
the word the bills use; a single mention counts beside biological sex
the person's own phrase; 'ban' is not a subject
a plural the table owns still finds the title with its singular
the plural of a slang word is the plant: 23 cannabis bills were listed while the table took the s off

not the family court's 'parental rights and responsibilities'

neither title says it; both texts do
